bullets.title: SNOW: Blowout Q2 drives +22% surge; Citi raises PT to $490, tracking to +40% 2H growth
bullets.body: SNOW reported product revenue +37% y/y with cRPO accelerating to +42% y/y; 2H guidance raised 6-7 pts and operating margin expanded to 15%+. Citi raised PT to $490 (from $395) citing AI flywheel via Cortex/Copilot. MS notes path to +40% growth in 2H26 with FY27 guided +36%, while Hedgeye/Wolfe both flagged the name as a high-conviction long going into the print.

bullets.title: AVGO: FY28 AI revenue guided to $230B (vs. ~$200B buy-side); stock -3% on mixed near-term reaction
bullets.body: AVGO reported F3Q26 AI revenues of $16.7B (+221% y/y) with XPU shipments >3.5x y/y; Oct-Q AI guidance $21.7B (+30% q/q). FY27 AI framework doubles to $115B and FY28 doubles again to $230B with $30 EPS guide. JPM maintains OW/$580 PT; Rosenblatt raised PT to $600 from $500. Despite the long-term beat, stock traded -3% as near-term optics were mixed and buy-side consensus was already ~$200B for FY28.

bullets.title: CRWD: Fal.Con confirms AI security opportunity; $10B ARR pulled forward to FY30, NNARR +20% target
bullets.body: Citi reaffirms Buy/$260 PT after Fal.Con; CRWD introduced AI Guardian and SafeMind products with token-based pricing. FY29 $10B ARR and FY34 $20B ARR targets pulled forward 1-2 years; FY28 NNARR growth target set at 20%+ (roughly double prior consensus). Falcon Guardian priced significantly above prior AIDR SKU, potentially a $250M+ SKU representing 15-20% of FY28E NNARR. SafeMind models show 29-37% better detection at 99% lower cost vs. general-purpose models.

bullets.title: CIEN: FY27 guidance +30% to $8.3-8.4B; supply-constrained through 2028, Hyper-Rail ramping
bullets.body: CIEN Q3 revenue $1.67B beat ($1.64B est), EPS $2.11 vs $1.73. FY27 revenue guided +30% y/y to $8.3-8.4B with gross margins 45-46% and operating margins 25-27% (vs. consensus 22.7%). Backlog expected to exceed $10B at FY26 year-end; supply/demand not expected to balance before 2028. JPM maintains OW, noting FY27 EPS implied at $11-12 vs. consensus $9.65. Hyper-Rail ramps to hundreds of millions in 2027 with above-average margins.

bullets.title: HPE: Beat and raise on AI inferencing; -12% on stock as FY27 growth guides 13-17% but supply constraints persist
bullets.body: HPE Q3 EPS $1.11 vs $0.93 est; raised FY26 EPS to $3.75-3.85 and FY27 EPS growth +16-20% y/y. Cloud & AI operating margin expanded to 17% from 7% y/y. Normalized order growth +42% y/y; $3.5B hyperscaler inferencing win and Oracle OCI networking deal. Despite strong results, stock -12% as Piper Sandler sees potential peak revenues/margins; supply constraints expected into 2027. Citi raised PT to $76, Truist to $70, Piper Sandler cut to $57.

bullets.title: NVDA: Bullish technical setup; Nscale/$3.5B Vera Rubin deal adds demand signal
bullets.body: Hedgeye flagged NVDA as a top long with bullish trade setup; 535,000+ 225 calls traded intraday. Nscale announced a $3.5B initial GPU commitment (scaling to $6B+) using NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform with up to 100,000 GPUs, deploying from H2 2027 in Texas. Hedgeye Risk Range bullish with buy target $209, sell target $231.

bullets.title: AVGO/GOOGL: Multi-year take-or-pay LTA cements AVGO vs. Mediatek; GOOGL deploying 5 GW TPU v8i in 2027
bullets.body: AVGO has a multi-year take-or-pay LTA with Google worth tens of billions per year; management believes Marvell's Google engagement is on adjacent products, not core TPU. GOOGL plans to ship multi-tens of billions in TPUs annually and a major AI lab will deploy 5 GW TPU v8i in 2027, with 10 GW incremental in 2028.

bullets.title: MSFT: Re-segmentation improves Azure transparency; SaaS (TEAM/NOW/CRM) as AI execution layer
bullets.body: MSFT restructured into two segments (Agents & Infra, Devices & Consumer), making Azure a cleaner consumption KPI with quarterly disclosure. Jefferies notes Infrastructure Software seeing strongest net buying post-SNOW earnings, with Application Software also seeing continued HF buying. NOW AI Control Tower has >500 live customers within six months with AI ACV exceeding $1B; TEAM MCP calls grew ~400% in the quarter with combined MCP/CLI users surpassing 1M.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 foldable launch Sept 9; $2,000+ Ultra pricing drives ASP uplift; TSMC sole A20 supplier
bullets.body: iPhone 18 launches Sept 9 with foldable 'iPhone Ultra' at $2,000+ and Pro/Pro Max ~$200 above predecessors. Citi forecasts 61.8M iPhone 18 units in 2H26 and 7.5M foldable units. TSMC is sole supplier of A20 2nm chips with Apple modem replacing Qualcomm. Supply chain underperformed Jun-Aug restocking; Citi expects pre-launch rally followed by post-launch profit-taking.

bullets.title: META: Muse Spark 1.3 achieves near-parity with OpenAI/Anthropic at lower cost; bullish trade but bearish trend
bullets.body: META Muse Spark 1.3 offers intelligence index 62 vs Anthropic Opus 5 Max's 63, consumes 25% fewer tokens and 20% fewer tool calls vs prior version, at significantly cheaper pricing. Citi notes Muse 1.3 is beating GOOGL's Gemini 3.8 Flash. Hedgeye flags META as bullish on trade but bearish on trend; Hedgeye Risk Range bearish with buy $547, sell $599.

bullets.title: DELL: Traditional server units down YoY; FY28 outlook flat-to-down units with ASP growth as key driver
bullets.body: DELL traditional server units declined YoY in the quarter (market down 9% YoY), with Gen 18 servers replacing 5-7 older units due to density improvements. FY28 outlook expects flat-to-down server units with ASP growth from richer configs and elevated memory pricing. AI servers will drive ISG growth but carry lower margins than traditional server business.

bullets.title: AXON: Flock controversy immaterial; only 5% agency AI adoption leaves 30% multi-year growth runway
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains OW/$640 PT on AXON; ALPR/Flock represents <1% of revenue and is immaterial to guidance. Only ~5% of 17,000 US agencies have adopted the full AI Era Plan; Draft One is the primary entry point with $200/officer/month bundle seen following OSP monetization path. Company reiterates 2028 targets of $6B revenue and 28% adjusted EBITDA margin.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Ad tech breakup denied; YouTube under FTC probe; Waymo leads vs. TSLA Cybercab at 4,000 vehicles
bullets.body: Federal judge denied DOJ bid to force GOOGL ad tech breakup, imposing behavioral remedies instead; GOOGL agreed to $353M UK app developer settlement. TSLA Cybercab event in Austin today with 200+ unsupervised vehicles vs. GOOGL Waymo's ~4,000 driverless vehicles. GOOGL Gemini also saw elevated error reports starting ~9AM ET alongside OpenAI/Anthropic outages.

bullets.title: AAPL/AMZN/GOOGL: Regulatory headwinds stack up across Big Tech
bullets.body: AAPL faces a $2.7B UK lawsuit over unfair app tracking rules imposing stricter requirements on third-party developers than Apple's own services. AMZN is being sued by FTC and 22 US states for allegedly raising advertiser prices without knowledge. ORCL is under EU antitrust scrutiny over licensing practices; RDDT and RBLX designated as very large platforms under strictest EU regulatory scrutiny.

bullets.title: CLS: +6.3% intraday on strength; outperforming TSX peers
bullets.body: Celestica (CLS.CN) trading +6.3% to C$408.55 in Canadian mid-morning session, one of the strongest performers on the TSX Composite (+0.79%). No specific catalyst cited beyond broad tech infrastructure strength.

bullets.title: TEAM/SNOW: Both hitting 52-week highs; SNOW +22.3% on day, TEAM +5.6%
bullets.body: SNOW reached $374.20, up +22.3% on the day and +60.2% on the 52-week period. TEAM hit $196.90, up +5.6% on the day and +14.0% over 52 weeks. Both lead the 52-week high list in the Technology Services sector.

bullets.title: AVGO/MRVL: Rosenblatt raises AVGO PT to $600 from $500; MRVL Google engagement seen as adjacent, not core TPU
bullets.body: Rosenblatt raised AVGO PT to $600 from $500 (63% upside vs. $367 current price). Separately, AVGO management believes Marvell's Google engagement is on adjacent products rather than core TPU displacement, reducing competitive concern.

bullets.title: VST: Named as power operator for CIFR's 2.5 GW lateral pipeline sites by end-2027
bullets.body: CIFR announced plans to develop lateral pipelines enabling up to 2.5 GW across multiple sites with power available before end of 2027; Vistra (VST) would operate power generation at those sites, building on existing Odessa relationship. Key uncertainty remains on timing and what 'up to' means for actual generation vs. pipe capacity.

bullets.title: AFRM: Citi FinTech Conference Nov 9-10; Mizuho reiterates Outperform/$100 PT on payments names
bullets.body: AFRM is among 40+ fintech firms presenting at Citi's 15th Annual FinTech Conference Nov 9-10 in NYC. Separately, Mizuho reiterates Outperform ratings on FISV ($78 PT), GPN ($110), and AFRM ($100) following FISV CEO meetings highlighting Project Elevate ($500M AI ops investment) with 10:1 pilot savings ratio.

bullets.title: Semiconductor tariff risk: Trump considering Section 232 expansion to servers/PCs; Phase 2 post Sept 24 Trump-Xi
bullets.body: The Trump administration is reportedly considering broadening Section 232 semiconductor tariffs beyond existing 25% to cover servers, PCs, and other electronics. Tariff Phase 2 announcement could follow the Trump-Xi meeting on September 24, with enactment likely January 2027 — a material risk for NVDA, DELL, HPE, AMD, and the broader semiconductor supply chain.
